subject.title: fix(browser): bound Playwright response body reads to prevent OOM

question: Should browser `responsebody` accept the new known-length oversized response contract: empty `body` with `truncated: true`, instead of preserving a truncated prefix?
rationale: The patch improves availability but changes the result shape for callers that previously received a prefix from oversized known-length responses, so automation should not choose the permanent compatibility contract.

options.title: Accept omitted-body contract
options.body: Land this PR with the empty-body `truncated: true` behavior because it avoids the known-large Buffer allocation and the CLI now explains the omission.

options.title: Preserve prefix compatibility
options.body: Remove the content-length early omit path and keep only the bounded decode mitigation if existing JSON/API prefix output matters more than avoiding the known-large Buffer allocation.

options.title: Hold for streaming design
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers require truly bounded capture for unknown-length responses without changing page response delivery.

recommendation.title: Accept omitted-body contract
recommendation.body: Land this PR with the empty-body `truncated: true` behavior because it avoids the known-large Buffer allocation and the CLI now explains the omission.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest browser responsebody and browser route ownership signal in current history.
